chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen from his brother al-Husayn from Ali ibn Yaqteen who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about speaking during the circumambulation (Tawaf), reciting poetry, and laughing, whether in the obligatory [pilgrimage] or the non-obligatory [pilgrimage]. Is that valid? He said, 'There is no harm with it, and poetry is [valid] if it is not harmful from it.'
And whoever forgets the Tawaf of Hajj until he returns to his people, then upon him is a camel (or a sacrifice), and upon him is the repetition of Hajj. He narrated that.

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A camel (used as a sacrificial offering)

ai.seo_question: Does speaking or laughing during Tawaf invalidate the Hajj, and what is the penalty for forgetting Tawaf al-Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that casual speech, poetry, and laughter do not invalidate Tawaf, provided the content is not frivolous or distracting, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease in ritual acts. It further specifies the penalty for forgetting Tawaf al-Hajj until leaving Mecca, requiring both a sacrificial animal (Badanah) and a return to perform the missed pillar, distinguishing it from mere omission. This ruling underscores the importance of Tawaf al-Hajj as a fundamental pillar (Rukn) of Hajj in Shia fiqh.
